overview: This file assembles U.S. diplomatic reporting, internal memoranda, newspaper clippings, translated press digests, and Japanese Dōmei bulletins documenting Japanese and Japanese-language media from 1940 to 1944. It traces the press’s movement from anti-Roosevelt cartoons and arguments against Anglo-American sanctions to full wartime propaganda promoting the Tripartite Pact, the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, Japanese military victories, and economic development under occupation. The collection also records U.S. monitoring of Japanese American newspapers during forced removal and incarceration, Japanese-language communities in Argentina, overseas propaganda distributed through Turkey, and Soviet and Chinese commentary on Japan as its wartime position deteriorated.
interest: Shows Japanese propaganda circulating through occupied Asia, Turkey, Argentina and immigrant communities, and US officials' skeptical evaluation of it.
